title: Hamish McRAE: Inflation is a stimulus to solve our finances
text:
By Hamish McRAe
Updated: 10:06 GMT, February 9, 2025
Inflation is climbing everywhere. The price of gold was quoted in a historical maximum of $ 2,886 per ounce of Troy on Friday, the sixth week in the trot.
There are many drivers, including uncertainty about Donald Trump’s commercial tariffs and the purchase of the Popular Bank of China.
But there is a primary reason, which is that investors worldwide believe that inflation can increase much more than the central banks will admit.
Here in the United Kingdom we can expect a strong increase in the consumer price index this year, and the Bank of England forecasts that will reach a maximum of 3.7 percent.
Its objective is 2 percent, so by rights it would expect interest rates, not reduce them.
We know why it is to reduce rates. See a serious recession, and that is all he can do.
Sagno and Sound: People who run the show (politicians, central bankers, senior officials, etc. are isolated from inflation
If the cheapest money will have a lot of effect is doubtful, because the reason why companies are reducing their labor forces and raising prices is the growing cost of using people, not at the cost of finance.
But I can understand that the bank does not want to blame if the economy is established.
It would not be totally fair to say that the bank has renounced inflation. But we have to assume that of its two monetary policy requirements, “maintaining prices stability” is somewhat lower in its priorities than the other, to support government policy, including its growth and employment objectives. “
There will also be greater inflation in the United States. The impact of tariffs is probably overvalued, because companies are quite good to work on ways of containing the load. Commercial adaptations. But he says in this way: commercial tariffs cannot reduce inflation and, on the sidelines, they must increase it.
The broader problem is what happens with monetary policy under the new administration of the United States.
The Federal Reserve is independent in regards to monetary policy, but it is an instrument of the United States government. So, to be realistic, you are not going to get in any blow if you can avoid it.
The new Treasury Secretary, Scott Besent, has calmed things a bit in saying that the administration approach will be Fed.
“He and I,” said speaking of the president, “we are focused on the Ten -year Treasury and what is the performance of that.”
If that is correct, Donald Trump will not push the Fed to reduce interest rates, as he did during his first mandate.
But real estate developers like Trump and are not too upset by inflation. In fact, they like inflation if that translates into higher values ​​for hotels and office blocks they are building.
So, if inflation initially increases by only a bit, it is likely that the Fed considers the increase in “transitory”, as it did in 2021, although given the disastrous result of its complacency, it will undoubtedly use any other expression to excuse its inaction .
The basic point is this. People who run the show (politicians, central bankers, senior officials, etc., are isolated from inflation. They are well paid. They have good pensions. Their salaries go up online or before price increases. They don’t have to worry about Fulfill the payroll.
So, if inflation rises to 3, 4 or 5 percent, that’s fine. They can say that their actions are ‘supporting the economy’ or some of this type.
Progressive inflation brings more fiscal income because tax bands do not fit, so governments really like it.
The rest of us have to face. We have to ensure that our savings are protected, which means a propagation of investments that include being the owner of our houses, putting a replacement in investments related to capital, building a pension, all the things that the personal finance pages of this newspaper urge us to do. Some may want to buy gold, although it is a bit late for that.
It is not easy, but if there is a positive side between some quite dark clouds, knowing that inflation is here to stay should be a spur to solve our own finances … in marked contrast with the way our government behaves.
